office_does: The prosecuting attorney decides which crimes are charged and prosecutes them, handles the county's civil cases and advises county officials.
race_blurb: Two Republicans: incumbent Eric Eisinger, who took 54.1% in the primary, faces Julie Long, a 28-year trial prosecutor and former chief deputy. Both run on enforcement; they differ over the incumbent's record on the charging backlog and office staffing.

candidates.summary: Benton County Prosecuting Attorney since 2023 and former private-practice litigator and Kennewick city prosecutor, endorsed by the county Republican Party and Sheriff Mike Clark.
highlights: Charges the highest provable offense, including firearm enhancements, and moves serious juvenile cases to adult court [S2]
Says prosecutor vacancies fell from five to one and the inherited felony backlog has been reduced [S4]
Says the office needs about twice its current number of criminal prosecutors and blames state underfunding [S4]
Supports veterans, drug, recovery and mental health courts for offenders willing to do the work [S2]

safety.basis: Runs on aggressive charging, bail, juveniles tried as adults and encampment removal; therapeutic courts are a secondary element.

experience.basis: Incumbent prosecutor since 2023 running on his first-term record, with 22+ years of litigation.

spending.basis: Argues the office needs roughly double its criminal prosecutors and more county money for victim services.

candidates.summary: Career deputy prosecutor in Benton and Franklin counties for 28 years, including more than 15 as chief deputy, challenging the incumbent over the charging backlog.
highlights: Pledges to prioritize a backlog of over 500 cases awaiting charging decisions [S1][S5]
Seeks high bail and no plea bargains with violent defendants; aggressive drug and gang prosecution [S1]
Supports therapeutic and veterans courts for appropriate candidates [S1]
Endorsed by former Sheriff Tom Croskrey, Sen. Nikki Torres, Commissioner Jerome Delvin and many retired officers [S4]

safety.basis: Repeatedly stresses high bail, ending lenient plea bargains and aggressive prosecution, with therapeutic courts only for suitable defendants.

experience.basis: Long institutional career as a line and chief deputy prosecutor, but has never held elected office and is challenging the incumbent.
